title: Aggregator receives 0 bundles — continues execution with empty result
problem: When 0 bundles reach an Aggregator and 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is OFF (the default), Make produces an empty aggregation result and passes it downstream. Downstream modules may silently receive an empty array or empty text, producing incorrect output without throwing an error.
symptoms: Aggregator outputs an empty result (empty array [], empty string, or 0) but no error is thrown
Downstream module (email, API write, report) executes with empty data
Scenario completes successfully but produces incorrect or blank output

likely_causes.cause: Upstream search or list module returned 0 records for this execution
A filter between the source and the Aggregator rejected all bundles
'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is disabled — the default Make behavior

diagnosis_steps: Open the execution and check how many bundles the module feeding the Iterator produced
Verify whether 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is disabled in the Aggregator settings
Add a filter after the Aggregator to check the output length before passing to downstream modules
Check whether a filter before the Aggregator rejected all bundles

solutions.solution: Enable 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' in the Aggregator settings if downstream modules should not run when the result is empty
solutions.conditions: When receiving empty aggregation should halt the scenario — this is the cleaner approach

solutions.solution: Add a filter after the Aggregator checking that the result length is greater than 0 before passing to downstream modules
solutions.conditions: When 'Stop processing' cannot be enabled and downstream modules must be guarded

prevention: Always handle the 0-result case after list or search modules before passing data into an Iterator + Aggregator chain
Test the scenario explicitly with queries that return 0 results to verify graceful handling

origin_details.evidence: Aggregator behavior confirmed in Make documentation. The silent nature of empty output (no error thrown) is inferred from Make's execution model and consistently reported in community. Not explicitly stated as a documented behavior in official source.

audit_notes: The 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' option is confirmed in Make documentation. The default behavior (continue with empty result) is confirmed. Entry split from the original vague entry to distinguish the two distinct behaviors.

evidence.claim: Make Aggregators continue execution by default when 0 bundles are received, producing an empty aggregation result
'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is a configurable option in Make Aggregator modules

conditions: Stop processing after empty aggregation = OFF

diagnostic_signals: Aggregator shows 0 bundles processed in execution history
Scenario completes with green status but target system shows no new data
Downstream module executed despite upstream returning 0 results

title: Aggregator stops processing on empty input — 'Stop processing after empty aggregation' enabled
problem: When 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is enabled in a Make Aggregator module and 0 bundles reach it, the Aggregator produces no output bundle at all and stops the processing route. Downstream modules do not execute. This is the intended behavior but may be unexpected if not configured deliberately.
symptoms: Downstream modules do not execute after an Aggregator that received 0 bundles
Execution history shows the Aggregator processed 0 bundles and the scenario stopped cleanly
No error is thrown — the behavior is intentional

likely_causes.cause: 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is enabled and the upstream produced 0 results

diagnosis_steps: Open the Aggregator module settings and check whether 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' is enabled
Check the upstream module to confirm whether 0 results is the expected behavior or an upstream error

solutions.solution: If downstream processing is required even when the aggregation is empty, disable 'Stop processing after an empty aggregation' and add a filter or Router to handle the empty case explicitly
solutions.conditions: When the stop behavior is unintentional and downstream should still run

prevention: Always handle the 0-result case after list or search modules before passing data into an Iterator + Aggregator chain
Test the scenario explicitly with queries that return 0 results to verify graceful handling
